source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: Chairman's letter cites accelerating expansion into Tier-2/Tier-3 cities and pilgrimage/leisure markets (Bharatpur, Trichy, Sindhudurg, Jawai, Wayanad) via the capital-light Ginger brand; Ginger revenue ~₹675 Cr of consolidated ₹8,565 Cr FY25 revenue. No explicit rural/tier-2-3 revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Overseas hotel operations generated ~₹1,512 Cr in FY25 against consolidated group revenue of ~₹8,565 Cr (~17.7%), implying foreign-currency revenue exposure; no explicit USD % or hedging policy disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (LMS) is positioned as a preferred global API/CDMO partner as global pharma diversifies away from China; company has acknowledged some API supply-chain dependence on China that it is calibrating via more Indian suppliers, aided by the PLI scheme. API business grew 14.6% sequentially in Q3 FY25, but growth attributed mainly to domestic and US markets rather than explicit China+1 diversification.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Interest coverage ratio improved to 14.6x in FY25 from 8.8x in FY24 and finance costs fell 5.4% YoY; fixed vs floating-rate debt split not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: US market was 36% of FY25 consolidated sales (USD 925 Mn vs USD 815 Mn FY24); broader USD-denominated revenue % and formal hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is an approved Group A applicant (domestic category) under India's PLI Scheme for critical KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs, per Dept. of Pharmaceuticals approved-applications list; specific revenue/incentive amount not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Primary AR PDF and IR site (ikshealth.com) were unreachable; third-party summaries consistently describe IKS Health as deriving roughly 90-95% of revenue from US healthcare clients (India-based delivery, USD-denominated revenue), with >90% from repeat/recurring clients. No AR-disclosed exact percentage or hedging policy confirmed.

rural.evidence: FY2024-25 press commentary: Powertrain Solutions division sales grew 5.8% 'fueled by rising exports and domestic tractor demand'; Q4 FY25 revenue grew 16% YoY driven by auto-market growth, mainly Tractor and Passenger Car segments. No rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Bosch Limited is reported as effectively debt-free (total debt/equity ~0.01 per Screener.in); no floating-rate liability disclosure found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary press summaries attribute profit improvement partly to 'reduction in material cost & budgetary control on expenses'; no raw-material-cost-as-%-of-revenue figure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Secondary reporting indicates Bosch Limited has not benefited from India's Auto PLI scheme the way some competitors have, and is described as working to raise domestic value addition toward the 50% minimum threshold required for PLI compliance.

rural.evidence: Dec-2024 quarter commentary attributed India sales growth partly to 'broader coverage in semi-urban and rural areas'; no rural % of revenue disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt reported at ₹25 Mn FY25 vs ₹13 Mn FY24; interest coverage improved to 60.4x from 47.5x, suggesting near-net-debt-free position at consolidated level; no floating/fixed split found.

inr_exposure.evidence: India business was 33% of FY25 revenue ('Largest Pharma company in India'); US business contributed 31% of FY25 revenue. Emerging Markets ($1,114M) and RoW ($847M) segments not separately confirmed as Europe/Asia splits.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma was not found on any retrieved PLI bulk-drug approved-beneficiary list; treated as not found rather than confirmed non-participant.

rate_sensitive.evidence: CARO disclosure: 'The Company did not have any outstanding loans or borrowings or interest thereon due to any lender during the year' and no term loans outstanding — effectively debt-free (only lease liabilities of ₹448.28 Mn).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedges trade receivables in major currencies (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, JPY) using forward contracts, tenor 30-120 days matched to expected collection period. Outstanding forward contracts as at Mar-2024: Sell USD 88.60mn, EUR 14.60mn, AUD 11.22mn, JPY 505.00mn, GBP 3.40mn. Net unhedged FX exposure ₹2,630.44 Mn (vs ₹1,332.90 Mn FY23).
inr_exposure.evidence: FY2023-24 Annual Report Note 25 (Disaggregate revenue): India ₹6,135.73 Mn (9.6%), USA ₹17,891.44 Mn (28.1%), Europe ₹9,319.95 Mn (14.6%), Asia Pacific ₹13,426.17 Mn (21.1%, not China-specific), Middle East/Africa + Rest of America ₹16,956.32 Mn (26.6%) of total ₹63,729.61 Mn.

rural.evidence: Analyst commentary notes consumption in Tier-2/3/4 cities and rural areas could outpace urban growth, which would benefit USL's distribution footprint; no management-disclosed rural % of revenue found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Finance costs reportedly decreased ~26.9% YoY in FY24; no floating vs fixed rate debt split found.

crude_exposure.evidence: CFO commentary cites ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass as the two biggest production cost components; glass bottle costs up 11-17%, paper cartons up ~100%, PET resin (petrochemical-linked) up 30-50%, plastic caps up 15-20% — directional petrochemical/packaging cost sensitivity, but no explicit %-of-raw-materials figure disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Unverified secondary source suggests exports ~8-10% of revenue to 37+ countries with a company target of 15% by 2026; not corroborated by a primary source. No hedging policy details found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party summary describes raw-material sourcing as 'primarily from domestic Indian suppliers supplemented by imports from key global partners in the United States, Germany, and Spain, while maintaining low direct exposure to high-risk regions like China' — not framed as a China+1 growth thesis, so rated none.

rural.evidence: Secondary sources describe an 'extensive pan-India distribution network, especially in tier-II and tier-III cities where advanced therapies are still underpenetrated' and rural-market distribution strength; no quantified rural % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Appears largely low-debt/net-cash (secondary sources cite net cash ~₹54.74bn and separately net debt ~₹414cr as of Sep-25); no floating vs fixed rate breakdown found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Unverified secondary source attributes to Alkem's CFO a statement that the company 'generally hedges about 80% of its forex exposure' — not confirmed against a primary transcript or AR.
inr_exposure.evidence: US business estimated ~22% of FY25 revenue per secondary/search-snippet sourcing (AR itself inaccessible).
US constant-currency revenue $35Mn in Q4FY25, up 10% YoY; US ~13% of FY24-25 group revenue per broker summaries (India incl. CRAMs 57%, Brazil 9%, US 13%, Germany 11%).

pli_scheme.evidence: No source referenced Torrent as a PLI (bulk drugs/API) beneficiary; characterized as a branded-formulations/generics company (~74% of FY24 sales from branded generics) rather than a bulk-API manufacturer typically associated with PLI.

rural.evidence: MD&A emphasizes 'Rurban' (rural + semi-urban) strategy; products reach ~209,050 villages, touching 2 of every 3 Indian households, direct rural reach ~1.5 million outlets (overall ~5.1 million). CMD highlighted rural as a strong growth opportunity in FY25. An older estimate (2021) pegged rural at ~25% of revenue, up from ~10% (2016), but no FY24-25-specific rural revenue % found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Minimal borrowings historically (~₹477 Cr in a recent quarter, likely largely lease liabilities); no explicit floating vs fixed rate breakdown found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Commentary notes 'edible oil prices are firm and have moved higher in line with global crude oil prices' and flags packaging cost inflation as a margin headwind alongside milk, coffee, cocoa, wheat. No specific % of raw material basket tied to crude/polymer disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (small revenue share) go to USA, Canada, Middle East, North Africa; FY25 introduced new export SKUs (KOKO KRUNCH, NESTLÉ GOLD cereals). No USD revenue % or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Cited as one of ~53 approved beneficiaries under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), a ₹10,900 Cr central scheme partly aimed at boosting exports; specific incentive amount received not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Analyst commentary notes Radico continues to dominate semi-urban and rural segments with trusted value brands while premiumizing via P&A brands (Rampur, Jaisalmer, Royal Ranthambore); no numeric rural revenue split disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are grain, ENA (partly captive via new Sitapur 350 KLPD ENA distillery) and glass bottles (recycled glass share raised from 4.5% in FY19 to 20.8% in FY24 for key brands); FY24 gross-margin pressure attributed to grain/ENA/glass price volatility, no explicit crude-oil/petrochemical linkage found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international business (Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, duty-free/airport retail across ~100 countries) is ~8-9% of FY25 revenue and 4-5% of volume; no specific USD hedging/forward-contract policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence of PLI participation; India's PLI schemes target electronics, pharma, textiles, solar and auto components, not alcobev/IMFL.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing found for FY24-25; Glenmark divested its API business (Glenmark Life Sciences, sold to Nirma in FY23-24), which previously carried the China+1 API narrative. Post-divestment, Glenmark is framed around branded/generics/OTC formulations, not API diversification.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Borrowings reduced sharply (~₹2,473 Cr as of Mar-2025); no floating-vs-fixed split found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: CFO commentary indicates reliance on natural hedging for currency exposure rather than extensive forward-contract hedging; no forward-contract % or formal hedging ratio found.
inr_exposure.evidence: North America (~23.85% of FY25 revenue, ₹31,771 Mn) and Europe (~21.36%, ₹28,463 Mn) are the main foreign-currency-linked revenue of ₹1,33,217 Mn total.

pli_scheme.evidence: Glenmark was one of 9 domestic companies approved in Group A of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (formulations track, ~₹11,000 Cr of ₹15,000 Cr Group A allocation). The separate bulk-drugs/API PLI scheme was more relevant to the divested Glenmark Life Sciences entity. No specific FY24-25 revenue % or incentive amount found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' phrase used. MD&A/GCEO letter frames Sona Comstar as 'emerging as a strategic partner of choice in a reshaped global supply chain' amid US tariffs/trade tensions, citing supply-chain diversification aligned with India's industrial growth. Revenue mix: North America 41%, India 29%, Europe 24%, Asia 6%. Company is also expanding into China/Asia (not purely diversifying away from it), so framing stops short of explicit China+1 attribution.

govt_capex.evidence: Railway Equipment Division of Escorts Kubota acquired (deal closed 1-Jun-2025, after FY25 close); MD&A notes increasing government capex/budgetary support for railway network expansion as a forward-looking driver, not yet reflected in FY25 revenue.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net cash company: total debt fell to ₹135 Mn (Mar-2025) from ₹2,331 Mn (Mar-2024); net cash of ₹26,591 Mn after a ₹23,695 Mn QIP. Notes disclose 'Variable rate borrowings' equal to total borrowings in both years (100% floating, T-bill linked, ~9.15% p.a. effective FY24 rate); by FY25 year-end borrowings were largely repaid.

crude_exposure.evidence: Material cost was 43% of total income in both FY2024-25 and FY2023-24 (₹15,447 Mn). Inputs are special steel alloy bars, iron castings, steel blanks/bolts, copper enamelled wires, machined aluminium die castings, bearings, magnets, plastic moulded components — steel/metal forging inputs, not literal crude oil; no explicit oil-price-linked commentary found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy primarily using forward contracts to hedge currency risk on USD/EUR export sales and foreign-currency purchases.
inr_exposure.evidence: Outstanding forward contracts at 31-Mar-2025: USD 109.55mn and EUR 20.81mn (receivable side). 41% figure is North America revenue share used as a USD-exposure proxy; currency-specific revenue % not separately disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review: 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.' Board's Report cites PLI certification for its electric two-wheeler traction motor under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. No PLI incentive amount quantified as % of revenue.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Annual report / Notes to Accounts were not directly accessible. Third-party earnings-call summaries (unverified) indicate average cost of borrowing fell to ~8.5% in FY25 from ~9.2% in FY24, gross debt ~₹4,400 Cr, net debt/EBITDA ~1.2x as of Q4 FY25; no floating-vs-fixed split found.

rural.evidence: No consolidated company-wide tier-2/3/rural revenue % located. Third-party summaries describe Tier-II/III cities growing faster than Tier-I; retail footprint expanded from 63 stores in 34 cities (FY2020) to 237 stores in 79 cities (FY2025), with roughly half of FY25's ~50 new offline stores in Tier-II/III markets. The eB2B Superstore channel (276k retailers across 1,100+ cities) derives a large share of sales from Tier-2+ cities, but this is specific to the B2B wholesale channel, not total consolidated revenue.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party summaries note long-term debt rose to roughly ₹1 Bn in FY25 (from near-zero FY24) and finance costs rose ~29.5% YoY; no floating-vs-fixed borrowing split found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found of Nykaa or any owned-brand manufacturing subsidiary participating in a PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/investor language cites 'building capacities in a few more niche APIs as per the evolving demand scenario in the backdrop of China plus one opportunities.' Also referenced in connection with the US Biosecure Act, positioning Divi's as 'a top candidate for these redirected contracts' given its clean USFDA record. Kakinada Unit-3 came online (~Jan 2025) cited as strengthening backward integration and supply-chain resilience. No specific quantified order-book growth tied explicitly to China+1 found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net-cash company: negative net debt of ~₹7,427 Cr as of Mar-2025 (improved from ₹7,959 Cr Mar-2024), i.e. cash exceeds borrowings. No floating vs fixed rate borrowing split found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Strategy of backward integration, solvent recovery, in-house utilities, and raw-material diversification away from China cited to manage input costs; no explicit crude-oil-price linkage found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share ~87-88% of revenue (Europe ~52.3% of gross sales, North America ~17.1%) implies high USD/EUR exposure; 9M-FY25 forex gain of ₹38 Cr (vs ₹32 Cr 9M-FY24). No specific hedge ratio or forward-contract notional found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not confirmed on published PLI-for-KSMs/APIs approved-applicant lists. Divi's independently backward-integrated into KSMs (Gabapentin, Naproxen, Valsartan, Levetiracetam) during FY19-FY21 to cut China import dependency, but this predates/is separate from formal PLI approval.

rural.evidence: A FY24 (not FY25) secondary source citing an equitymaster AR-analysis summary stated '53% from Tier-6 cities and rural areas and 47% from other segments' — wrong fiscal year and unverified against primary AR text, so not used as a confirmed FY25 fact.

pli_scheme.evidence: Industry-wide fact only: 'In FY25, the government disbursed ₹2,328 Cr under the pharma PLI schemes' (sector-wide, not Mankind-specific). No source confirms Mankind Pharma itself as a named PLI beneficiary.

India's PLI-Auto Scheme exists generically (Cabinet-approved 2021, ₹25,938 Cr outlay, FY2022-23 to FY2026-27), but no source found confirms Endurance Technologies as a named beneficiary; AR PDF, IR site, and jina.ai proxy all returned HTTP 403 within the fetch budget.

govt_capex.evidence: Qualitative commentary only: 'sustained increase in demand' from infrastructure and mining sectors; wire rope segment = 72% of FY25 revenue (71% FY24), with value-added categories (crane, oil & offshore, elevator, mining, fishing) = 71% share within wire ropes. No % tied specifically to government/public-sector orders disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Deleveraging trend noted (a later-period report references repaid borrowings of ₹192 Cr and 'debt-free standalone status', but this appears to reference the period after FY25). FY25 year-end floating/fixed debt split not confirmed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International markets = 55% of FY25 consolidated revenue (₹3,474 Cr total, up 7.7% from ₹3,225 Cr FY24), driven by 9.5% volume growth and export strength. Region breakdown (US/Europe/Asia-ex-China/other) and hedging policy not disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found linking Usha Martin to the Specialty Steel PLI scheme (2023-24 to 2027-28).
